As a UX/Ul Designer, I was responsible for designing four main interfaces for this project: the main website, user dashboard, admin
dashboard, and mobile app all created using Figma.
My responsibilities included designing multiple screens and user flows for each platform version to ensure a smooth and intuitive
experience. I also built the design foundation by creating a typography system, color palette, layout grid, and several reusable
components to support responsive design across different devices.
The design process for this project was divided into four key phases to ensure a user centered and results experience:
In the discovery phase, I began by conducting a competitor analysis to understand how similar platforms approach ethical
investing and religious based screening tools. This helped identify design opportunities and areas for differentiation. I also
gathered insights into user pain points, particularly related to complexity in financial tools and the lack of moral transparency in
investment platforms. Additionally, I defined the target users and audience, which included faith driven individual investors and
administrative users who need to manage ethical investment data efficiently. These early findings shaped the direction for user
experience decisions in the next phases.
During the ideation phase, I focused on translating user needs into clear pathways by creating the user flow and user journey
maps. This helped visualize how users would interact with the platform, from discovering the website to monitoring their
investment portfolios or managing users in the admin panel. These artifacts ensured that each user role - admin and user -
had a smooth and logical navigation structure, minimizing friction and enhancing usability across all interfaces.
To maintain visual consistency and scalability, 1 developed a design system in Figma that included the core elements such as
color palette, typography scale, grid system, and a component set consisting of buttons, inputs, cards, and other Ul elements.
The system was tailored for both web and mobile use, with responsive behavior in mind. I also built specific component
variations for different features within the user and admin dashboards, ensuring clarity and ease of reuse throughout the
In the usability testing phase, I created a set of task and scenarios to simulate how users would interact with the platform in real
world contexts. These scenarios were designed to evaluate the clarity of navigation, the effectiveness of information hierarchy,
and the intuitiveness of key actions like creating a portfolio or filtering ethical concerns. While the testing was limited to scenario
creation, it laid a strong foundation for future validation and iteration with actual users.
Before diving into design, I started by understanding the purpose and values behind the platform. Sanctify was developed as a
solution for investors who want their financial portfolios to align with Catholic moral principles. This meant not only building a
functional and trustworthy interface, but also clearly communicating the value of ethical investment screening. My goal during this
discovery phase was to understand the unique positioning of the product, uncover common pain points in existing tools, and
explore how to design a product that resonates with both faith-driven users and platform admins.
To gain insights into the current landscape of faith based or ethical investing tools, I analyzed several platforms that offer screening,
portfolio monitoring, or ethical investing support. The goal was to identify design patterns, messaging strategies, and opportunities

beginning to end while addressing user needs around ethical clarity, ease of understanding, and trust in the platform. This stage
resulted in the development of user flows and a comprehensive journey map to ensure alignment between user expectations and
To ensure a clear and intuitive user experience, I created user flows that reflect the typical paths a user might take, starting from
main website, user dashboard, and admin dashboard. Each flow was designed with simplicity in mind, highlighting key interactions
such as filtering ethical categories, tracking portfolio performance, and add new user for admin version. The user flow also
accounted for both first time visitors and returning users with different goals, whether it's ethical discovery or portfolio optimization
User story: As a investor, I want to add a screen set that provides maximum profit potential and minimizes risk, so that I can make more
profitable investment decisions based on my market research.
User story: As an admin, I want to be able to add other admin users easily, so that I can share the work with my partner
User story: As a new user, I want to be able to get information easily, so that I can trust Sanctify and feel confident becoming a user
A user journey map was developed based on a realistic scenario. This journey explores their experience from discovering Sanctify
for the first time to using the platform to build a morally responsible portfolio. The map outlines their actions, thoughts, emotional
state, and key opportunities to improve their experience at each stage. This helped identify critical moments where Ul clarity,
educational content, and interactive elements could influence user trust and decisional making.

This section showcases the Add Screenset flow on the Sanctify platform. Although this feature is also available on the desktop
version, only the mobile version is presented here due to its simpler and more compact layout, which allows all four pages to be
displayed within a single section. The following is a walkthrough of how the Add Screenset process works in Sanctify, starting from
the leftmost page and progressing to the right.
Users begin the process on the first screen, Add Screen, where they can select a category and relevant screener through dropdown
menus. The clean and minimalist interface allows users to focus on selecting the appropriate screening content, such as "Adult
Content Provider" or "Adult Content Distribution." Once a screener is selected, users can tap the green "Add Screen" button to
After the screener has been added, users are directed to the second screen, Add Screenset Sets Value. In this stage, all previously
selected screeners are displayed and grouped under categories such as Environment, Smoking, and Weapons. Each screener is
accompanied by a percentage field that allows users to assign a weight or impact value based on their specific ethical policies. A
delete icon is available next to each item, offering flexibility in managing the list. This screen provides granular control, enabling
users to fine tune the screening values before tapping the "Save Screen Set" button to save their configuration.
Next, users move on to the third screen, Add Screenset, where they name the set of screeners they've just configured. A
comprehensive list of available screeners is shown, again grouped by categories such as Adult Content, Environment, and Medical
Ethics. Users can make further selections or revisions at this stage. Once finalized, they can press the "Save and Continue" button
Finally, users arrive at the fourth screen, Research Details, which presents a detailed report of the screenset they created. At the
top, users can select which screenset to review (e.g., "FFV Scorecard") using a dropdown. The report is visually organized into
separate cards by category, like Weapons and Environment, each displaying a letter grade (such as A or D) along with progress bars
that reflect specific percentage scores. This layout allows for quick and intuitive assessment of ethical and sustainability
performance. At the bottom of the screen, users are prompted to upgrade to a paid plan once their 14 day free trial ends, with a
green "View Pricing Plan" button leading to subscription options.
Overall, this four step flow is designed to guide users through the process of building, customizing, and analyzing ethical screensets
with precision and ease, especially in a mobile context that emphasizes simplicity and usability
For this usability testing, I crafted a series of task based scenarios that simulate real user interactions flow on Sanctify's platform.
The purpose of this testing session was to observe how users understand and navigate through each step of the flow. The tasks
and scenarios were designed to reflect realistic goals and decision making contexts, allowing participants to engage with the
prototype as if they were using the live product. By placing users in relevant scenarios, I was able to collect authentic feedback on
usability, comprehension, and overall interaction quality.
This testing was not limited to identifying surface level issues like button placements or visual clarity, but also aimed to uncover
deeper usability challenges such as flow continuity, language clarity, and user confidence in decision making.
The usability testing was conducted using a high fidelity prototype, and participants were asked to think aloud while performing the
tasks. Their input, behaviors, and pain points were carefully observed and documented. Insights gained from this phase informed
the next iteration of the design. So, this process ensured that each design decision was rooted in real user behavior and contributed
to building a more intuitive and accessible product.
If given more time, I would further refine Sanctify by taking the following steps:
1. Conducting additional user research to uncover deeper usability concerns or ethical decision making behaviors that may not
have surfaced in the initial phase. This would allow me to gain more meaningful insights from users, particularly in how they
interpret and interact with Sanctify's screening and scoring features.
2. Carry out usability testing based on the predefined tasks and scenarios developed for the "Add Screenset" flow. This testing
would help evaluate the clarity of information hierarchy, the ease of navigation across multiple steps, and the overall confidence
users feel when configuring and reviewing ethical screeners.
3. Based on findings from evaluations, I would identify pain points or areas of friction, then prioritize solving them to enhance
usability. Improvements would be directed toward making the experience more seamless, intuitive, and aligned with the
expectations of users who are likely to approach the platform with a professional or analytical mindset.
4. Continue iterating on both the visual and functional aspects of the design, refining the interface to ensure consistency, improving
microinteractions, and strengthening the platform's ability to deliver complex screening data in a digestible, user centered way.
